name: PromptCBLUE
intro: PromptCBLUE是基于CBLUE重建的中文医疗领域大模型评测基准，评估中文大模型在医疗实体识别、文本分类、自然语言推理、对话理解及内容生成等多任务上的能力，提供在线评测平台。
build_method: 将16项中文医疗NLP任务改造成统一提示—回答生成格式；人工种子经医疗/NLP专家审核后由ChatGPT改写并再次审核，再按论文规则抽样与质检
metric: 严格micro-F1, macro-F1, ROUGE-1/2/L, 任务平均分
task_type: 多任务（实体识别, 分类, 推理, 对话, 生成）
eval_feature: 隐藏测试target；共享LLM主干与语言模型头；任务专用文本后处理；在线平台评分
scale: 论文表8含16项任务：印刷总计为训练82,600、开发/测试各7,656，但16行实算为78,100/6,856/6,856，差额4,500/800/800且论文未解释；正文称每任务训练3,000–5,000条，但表8的CHIP-CTC为6,600、KUAKE-QIC为5,500，冲突同样未解释；仓库v0.2 README另报94个模板及68,900/10,360/10,320/10,320条
task_type_en: Multi-task (entity recognition, Classification, Reasoning, Dialogue, Generation)
build_method_en: Reformulate 16 Chinese medical NLP tasks as prompt-response generation; review manual seeds with medical/NLP experts, rephrase them with ChatGPT, review again, then sample and quality-check by the paper protocol
eval_feature_en: Hide test targets; require one shared LLM backbone and language-model head; apply task-specific text post-processing; score online
intro_en: PromptCBLUE is a Chinese medical large model evaluation benchmark reconstructed from CBLUE. It assesses the capabilities of Chinese large models across multiple tasks, including medical entity recognition, text classification, natural language inference, dialogue understanding, and content generation, and provides an online evaluation platform.

drawio_review_note: reviewed_at=2026-07-18; status=source-reconstructed-awaiting-independent-signoff; scope=PromptCBLUE paper-v1 construction plus the fixed official repository and CCKS/Tianchi evaluation contract. Primary paper evidence is https://arxiv.org/pdf/2310.14151v1 with SHA-256 2a69d5133e62e50395ae07a9ea5d6a108aa970a7bfc9c6b77443d25be6c6f0a0. Repository evidence is michael-wzhu/PromptCBLUE at commit b0753a61a7c1f4e1ae171109f8a59037ff0a5543. Supporting fixed-file hashes are templates.json 0aac544dcd52300265f7277c8668304e61572573ba7521278302045ee74231a7, templates_augment.json ad7cdad16ac4277e714dfbcf54180005fafd34141e31f9cfd658c5cf09f1f0d3, post_generate_process.py f9bad5ce70e5c41b164e9e597687515a036c6cef4722f95584e56b55dad8f05c, and evaluate.py 361f249819c7313cb23340c7c1d3ab787706e25c91436e68cfac35d6cbcad97f. Construction was checked against paper section 3.2 and Appendix A: the benchmark contains 16 Chinese medical tasks grouped as five information-extraction, three classification, four natural-language-inference, two symptom-status, and two generation tasks. Three computer-science graduate annotators each write about two diverse seed prompts; two medical experts and one senior NLP researcher review them and require revision until acceptance. ChatGPT then rephrases each of the six seeds ten times without changing meaning or placeholders, and the same panel accepts or rejects generated templates. Prompts may include label definitions, output-format instructions, demonstrations, and step-by-step instructions. Original spans, labels, and structures are serialized into text and emitted under input, target, answer_choices, sample_id, task_type, and task_dataset; only input and target define the model contract, while the other four are auxiliary. Each source sample is filled into templates to create a large pool. Section 3.2 then says each task is uniformly sampled to 3,000-5,000 training and 600-800 development/test items, but Table 8 lists 6,600 training items for CHIP-CTC and 5,500 for KUAKE-QIC; the paper does not reconcile this prose-versus-table conflict. Quality checks cover expert template review, feedback to CBLUE including QQR re-annotation, and medical review of 5% or 200 samples per task, reporting an average 0.9% mislabeling rate. A critical provenance boundary is explicit: Table 8's printed total reports 82,600/7,656/7,656 train/dev/test, while direct addition of its 16 task rows gives 78,100/6,856/6,856. The unexplained printed-minus-row gap is therefore 4,500/800/800; neither set of paper values is silently normalized. Separately, the fixed v0.2 README reports 68,900/10,360/10,320/10,320 train/dev/Test-A/Test-B. The README claims 94 templates, but the pinned files contain 91 entries in templates.json and 352 augmented entries in templates_augment.json; these are release observations, not silently substituted paper counts. Evaluation was checked end to end: disclosed settings are fixed same-task ICL demonstrations, few-shot fine-tuning, and full-data fine-tuning or PEFT. Competition rules require one shared LLM backbone and LM head across tasks and total PEFT parameters below 1%. Released test targets are empty; input must be fed verbatim while row count, order, and sample_id are preserved. The ZIP must contain test_predictions.json and a Python-standard-library-only post_generate_process.py at its root; the platform executes that parser and ignores a manually uploaded results.json. Strict instance micro-F1 scores extraction/status outputs, macro-F1 scores CHIP-CTC, KUAKE-QIC and IMCS-V2-DAC, micro-F1 scores CHIP-STS/KUAKE-QQR/KUAKE-IR/KUAKE-QTR, and character-spaced ROUGE-1/2/L scores generation, with six IMCS-V2-MRG report sections averaged. The leaderboard mean uses each of the 16 paper tasks' F1 or ROUGE-L. The fixed Git tree has no LICENSE file and full competition data is distributed through Tianchi, so the diagram does not invent reuse terms. EN/ZH specifications have identical positioned topology, no edge labels, dashed provenance edges, and were prepared for strict Draw.io/XML plus runtime visual review; formal assets and paper_aligned registration remain gated on independent approval.
